spec_match.rationale: The copy and sample use the current named-trigger grammar and clearly label both columns as illustrations, but standard CSS animations simulate rather than prove AnimationTrigger behavior.

interactive.rationale: Independent restart and no-rewind controls produce a clear repeated-trigger comparison.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index accurately describes the comparison's intended old-versus-new behavior.

edge_cases.rationale: Finished-forward behavior is illustrated; reverse direction and repeated opposite events are now covered additively by the press-release-feedback concept, while paused state and native trigger state remain absent here.

references.rationale: The canonical ChromeStatus feature and CSSWG specification are directly linked.

conformance.rationale: The visible inherited suite exposes the accepted but incorrect view() assertion and does not test the no-auto-rewind runtime contract. Flagged for a human: existing assertions are immutable and cannot be corrected by this routine.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Previously exercised via Chrome DevTools MCP at 390x844 and 1280x800 with clean console/network; this pass re-verified the feature route with the headless-Chrome parity harness (desktop and mobile OK) after adding the sibling concept.

telemetry_health.rationale: Shared interaction telemetry runs, but no page-specific native behavior assertion exists on this page; the new press-release-feedback sibling asserts the no-rewind contract.

design_system.rationale: Shared variables are used and the comparison collapses to one column at mobile width.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons and polite live result text expose each comparison state without relying on motion alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: One column at narrow width, two at desktop, no page overflow; re-confirmed via the responsive-check harness on 2026-08-16.

guidanceConsulted.query: Expose live feature detection and conformance test results as an accessible educational details interface
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic structure, native controls, concise status announcements, visible focus, and source-linked alternatives for visual state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied native controls, polite result regions, a mobile single-column layout, and the shared visible assertion panel.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Headless-Chrome harness run 2026-08-16 (desktop+mobile OK) plus the prior Chrome DevTools MCP session evidence.

summary: The major open question (build the ChromeStatus press/release motivation as an additive native-syntax use case) is answered by the new press-release-feedback concept: real directional CSS.supports probes, a labelled Web Animations model of play-forwards/play-backwards, and a no-rewind assertion, verified headlessly with pointer, keyboard, hammering, and reset sequences. This basic comparison route is preserved unchanged as the entry-level illustration.
